puzzles.description: The agent has a plan. Who signs off, and when? Drag the steps into order.

answer: 🤖 Agent updates the plan with the PM's corrections and builds the first feature from the plan

hints: Plan first, build second. Every agent step is followed by a human check.
The agent drafts, the PM reviews, then the agent fixes the plan and builds. A human checks the result.
Agent drafts → PM reviews → Agent updates the plan and builds → Squad checks.

puzzles.description: The coding agent's pull request has landed. Make the calls at each gate.

steps.question: The coding agent opened a pull request for the feedback form. What happens next?
options: AWS Security Agent reviews it against the organization's compliance and standards
Deploy straight to production to save time
Merge it. The agent wrote it, so it's fine
wrong: Nothing reaches production without passing the gates first.
Fast isn't the same as safe. Every PR gets reviewed, no matter who wrote it.
steps.after: Review started. Security shifts left: it's checked on the PR, not after launch.

steps.question: The AWS Security Agent flags: "Citizen email addresses are logged in plain text." What do you do?
options: Ignore it. It's only an email address
Merge now and fix it next sprint
Return it to the agent to remediate, then re-run the gate
wrong: Citizen email addresses are personal data. Treat them seriously.
A flagged finding blocks the merge. 'Next sprint' is how leaks happen.
steps.after: Fixed and re-reviewed. Nothing blocking now.

steps.question: The code no longer logs citizen email addresses in plain text. Who should merge this PR?
wrong: A clean review is input to a decision, not the decision itself.
The agent proposes. A human approves at every gate.

onComplete.subtext: The agent wrote it. AWS Security Agent checked it. A human approved it.

hints: Every PR gets reviewed, flagged issues get fixed before merging, and a human makes the final call.
Review first. Return flagged issues to the agent to remediate. An engineer merges.
Answers: Security Agent review → return it to the agent to remediate → an engineer merges.

puzzles.description: Day one in production and the alarm is firing. The AWS DevOps Agent found the cause. Select what you would approve, and leave the wrong moves off.

tasks.label: Accept the agent's root cause: pool size set to 1
tasks.wrong_text_off: AWS DevOps Agent tested its hypotheses against the logs, metrics and traces. This one held up. Accept it.

tasks.label: Approve the agent's fix PR (pool size → 50)
tasks.wrong_text_off: The fix is ready. It needs a human to approve it before it ships.

tasks.label: Ship the fix through the pipeline
tasks.wrong_text_off: Even urgent fixes take the normal path: PR, review, pipeline. No hand edits in production.

tasks.label: Restart the database and hope it goes away
tasks.wrong_text_on: A restart treats the symptom. The pool size is still 1, so it'll break again. Fix the root cause.

tasks.label: Add a check so this can't happen again
tasks.wrong_text_off: Every incident teaches something. Feed it back into planning so the next release is safer. That's the loop in AI-DLC.

hints: Read every switch. Most are good calls, but one is a shortcut that only hides the problem.
Accept the root cause, approve the fix, ship it properly and learn from it. Don't just restart and hope.
Switch ON 1, 2, 3, and 5. Leave 4 off. You never restart and hope, and you never edit production by hand.
